# THEORYs with `tags` `philosophy-of-technology`

*Topics — What a work is about. Nucleation holds whatever reading the owner files here, whether or not an Anthology of the SOTA topic could also hold it; instruction for ML practice belongs to the anthology (ADR-048). The words are seeded from the clusters the reading-time triage of 2026-09-25 found, and grow by decision.*

**Philosophy of technology** — what technology is and what it does to those who live with it — the autonomy of technique, technological determinism and the social shaping of technology, lock-in and practical compulsion, automation and deskilling, technical codes and the politics of artifacts, design that steers or captures its users, critical theory of technology and convivial tools. A technology's regulation stays with society-and-governance, a measured effect of one product with social-science and a verdict on what is owed with ethics, unless the work argues about technology as such; how software is built is software-engineering (group: philosophy; ADR-098).

| [THEORY-1835](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1835.md) | Rosa holds that social acceleration has three dimensions, technological acceleration, acceleration of social change and of the pace of life, forming a closed, self-propelling cycle in which standing still means falling behind, so that modern societies must accelerate and grow merely to keep their institutional status quo, a mode he later calls dynamic stabilization | Rosa (2003 article, Skimmed in [NOTE-1918](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1918.md); 2021 interview, read in [NOTE-1915](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1915.md)). Three dimensions; self-propelling cycle; dynamic stabilization, the later name. A stand-in for [LIT-2566](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2566.md); corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1838](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1838.md) | Kelly argues that technology taken as a whole, the technium, is an interdependent, organism-like system whose self-reinforcing feedback gives it long-run tendencies independent of human wants, toward diversity, efficiency, complexity, ubiquity and interdependence, which on balance widen human choices | Kelly (2009 post, the thesis of the 2010 book), read in [NOTE-1947](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1947.md); the book's prologue in [NOTE-1943](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1943.md). The technium's tendencies; more ways, more choices. A foil to [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md): it measures the adopter's options. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1839](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1839.md) | Crawford holds that attention has become a collective, cultural problem because shared spaces treat people as a captive audience whose mental space can be monetized, that distraction is a problem of political economy rather than of technology in itself, and that attention should be protected as an attentional commons by those who design shared environments | Crawford (2017), an interview read in full in [NOTE-1938](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1938.md). A first-hand stand-in for the diagnosis of The World Beyond Your Head ([LIT-2574](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2574.md)). Corroborates [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md) as a reported case: smart cities whose controllers hold discretion over captive, dependent citizens. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1840](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1840.md) | Postman holds that technological change is a trade-off whose costs and benefits fall unevenly, that each technology carries an ideological bias that reshapes a culture's terms, that its effects are ecological, vast, often unpredictable and largely irreversible, and that technologies become mythic, accepted as natural and hard to control |  | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1841](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1841.md) | Feenberg argues that technology is neither neutral nor determined, that its design embodies a contingent technical code reflecting the values of dominant groups, that technological development is a field of social struggle with many feasible outcomes, and that an economic code that rewards deskilling could be replaced by one that values skill | Feenberg (2002), Preface and ch. 6, Skimmed in [NOTE-1927](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1927.md). Contingent technical code; deskilling as a code's choice. Corroborates [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1842](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1842.md) | Zuboff argues that surveillance capitalism is an institutional order that commodifies behaviour, concentrating knowledge about people in a few firms, so that epistemic inequality and a power to modify behaviour arise that compete with democratic governance and leave people practically without exit | Zuboff (2022), Skimmed in [NOTE-1928](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1928.md). Epistemic inequality; instrumentarian power; no exit. A stand-in for [LIT-2598](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2598.md); a worked case corroborating [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1843](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1843.md) | Han argues that the power maintaining the neoliberal system is seductive rather than repressive, exploiting freedom instead of suppressing it, making people dependent and each a self-exploiting entrepreneur, so that there is no one to resist and the subjugated do not experience themselves as subjugated | Han (2014), read in [NOTE-1929](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1929.md). Seductive power; dependence with no one opposite. A stand-in for [LIT-2567](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2567.md); it marks the limit of [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1844](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1844.md) | Crawford argues that skilled manual work is cognitively demanding and a ground of agency, and that work is degraded cognitively, by moving judgment out of the job into management or a system so that skilled workers can be replaced by cheaper ones, a method competition spreads across an industry and expert systems now carry into office work | Crawford (2006), read in [NOTE-1932](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1932.md). Deskilling as relocation of judgment. A stand-in for [LIT-2608](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2608.md); corroborates [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md) and [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1846](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1846.md) | Lanier holds that cybernetic totalism, the application of computer-science metaphors to people and reality, spreads through software design and grows the digital hive at the expense of individuality, and that information is alienated experience, which means nothing without a person to interpret it | Lanier (2010), You Are Not a Gadget, read in the publisher's excerpt of chapter 2 ([NOTE-1948](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1948.md), Skimmed). The book's own statement of the stance its predecessor essay states ([THEORY-1858](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1858.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1847](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1847.md) | Vallor holds that moral virtues are habituated and presuppose repeated practice of skills of moral analysis, deliberation and action, so that automated warfare which makes those practices redundant risks a moral deskilling of the military profession even with a human on the loop, since expertise to supervise a decision requires having practised it, and that whether a technology deskills is an empirical question of its context of use | Vallor (2013), read in full in [NOTE-1926](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1926.md). First-hand stand-in for her 2015 paper ([LIT-2599](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2599.md)) and for the deskilling thesis of The AI Mirror ([LIT-2591](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2591.md)). Corroborates [CLAIM-675](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-675.md)'s premise first-hand, which Adewuyi's review ([THEORY-1857](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1857.md)) gave second-hand. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1848](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1848.md) | Dijkema reads Crawford as holding that distraction dissolves individuality and freedom because modern epistemology relocated truth inside the head, leaving attention open to those who monopolize it, and that the remedy is an ecology of attention found in communities of skilled practice, where competence rests on an apprehension of real features of the world | Dijkema (2015), a review read in full in [NOTE-1939](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1939.md). A second-hand stand-in for the positive account of The World Beyond Your Head ([LIT-2574](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2574.md)). The reviewer's own call for authority is his, not Crawford's. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1849](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1849.md) | Farr reads Marcuse as holding that advanced industrial society sustains a democratic unfreedom in which domination takes the form of administration and needs neither force nor an authority figure, because the society makes people think themselves freer than they are and integrates them through needs it creates | Farr (SEP) on Marcuse, with Kellner, Skimmed in [NOTE-1931](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1931.md). Domination without an authority figure. A stand-in for [LIT-2560](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2560.md); it marks the limit of [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1851](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1851.md) | Benjamin argues that new technologies often reproduce and deepen existing racial hierarchies while promoted as more objective or progressive than older discriminatory systems, because designers encode social judgments into technical systems, including by default, and then treat the results as external to the design | Benjamin (2019), Introduction, Skimmed in [NOTE-1940](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1940.md). The New Jim Code; default discrimination. It marks the limit of [CLAIM-682](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-682.md)'s threshold. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1853](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1853.md) | Marcuse holds that advanced industrial society contains qualitative change by satisfying needs it has itself produced, false needs superimposed by particular social interests, so that domination takes the form of a comfortable administration in which technology rather than terror integrates people, the apparatus's apparent impersonality veils the interests that organize it, and its administrators are enclosed by it too | Marcuse (1964), read in full in [NOTE-1924](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1924.md) from the copy on the Marcuse family's site. Domination through satisfaction; control exercised through the choice of a society's project, veiled, by controllers enclosed in what they control. | [THEORY-1854](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1854.md) | Crawford and Joler argue that even a small AI device rests on a planetary system of extraction of minerals, labour and data, whose value concentrates in a very thin layer, and that transparency without real choice and corporate accountability does not change the resulting power asymmetry | Crawford and Joler (2018), read in [NOTE-1917](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1917.md). AI as extraction; transparency not enough. A stand-in for [LIT-2593](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2593.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1855](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1855.md) | Morozov argues that solutionism, recasting political and moral problems as technical problems to be optimized with sensors, data and incentives, leaves structural causes untouched, displaces moral motivation, and can make a nominally voluntary technology such as self-tracking a penalty on those who decline it | Morozov (2013 talk), read in [NOTE-1919](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1919.md). Solutionism; the self-tracking penalty. A stand-in for [LIT-2606](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2606.md); corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1856](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1856.md) | Vallor holds that calling AI superhuman is an ideology that, by redefining intelligence as outperforming humans at economically valuable work, devalues human agency and autonomy and erases the difference between human minds and the tools built to mirror them, and that the poverty of such tools may instead prompt a reclamation of humane capacities | Vallor (2024), Noema, read in full in [NOTE-1934](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1934.md). | [THEORY-1858](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1858.md) | Lanier argues that cybernetic totalism, the cluster of beliefs that people are information patterns, that subjective experience does not matter, that Darwinian algorithms describe all creativity and that computing power will soon bring a cataclysm, is a dogma, that real software resists improvement through legacy and lock-in, and that criticizing the dogma is not rejecting digital technology | Lanier (2000), "One Half a Manifesto", read in [NOTE-1946](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1946.md). Cybernetic totalism as dogma; legacy and lock-in; a humanist stance toward digital technology. A stand-in for You Are Not a Gadget ([LIT-2582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2582.md)). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1859](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1859.md) | Winner holds that artifacts can embody forms of power and authority in two ways, by a design or arrangement that settles an issue in a community and as inherently political technologies that require, or are strongly compatible with, particular political relations, and that the latitude of choice is greatest when a technology is first introduced and vanishes for practical purposes once initial commitments are made | Winner (1980), read in full in [NOTE-1941](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1941.md). A partial stand-in for Mumford's The Myth of the Machine ([LIT-2586](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2586.md)), for the distinction of authoritarian and democratic technics only. | [THEORY-1861](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1861.md) | Illich holds that industrial tools used to replace labour end by enslaving their users, that people need tools to work with rather than tools that work for them, that conviviality, individual freedom realized in personal interdependence, is an intrinsic ethical value, and that radical monopoly arises when one industrial process takes exclusive control of a pressing need and excludes non-industrial activity, as motor traffic curtails the right to walk | Illich (1973), a two-page excerpt Skimmed in [NOTE-1921](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1921.md); the whole book is Unfetched. Tools to work with against tools that "work" for people; conviviality; radical monopoly in Illich's own definition. | [THEORY-1862](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1862.md) | Cayley reads Illich as holding that tools, institutions included, become counterproductive past a second watershed and tend toward radical monopoly, the dominance of one kind of product that renders alternatives inaccessible or unimaginable, so that the test is whether one can still find an alternative or decently do without | Cayley (2021) on Illich, read in [NOTE-1922](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1922.md). Radical monopoly; the test of doing without. A stand-in for [LIT-2558](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2558.md); corroborates [CLAIM-677](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-677.md) and qualifies its title. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1863](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1863.md) | Illich holds that beyond a socially critical threshold of energy per person motorized transport reduces equity and establishes a radical monopoly, the dominance of an industry as the means of satisfying a need that formerly occasioned a personal response, imposed not by scarcity or by eliminating competitors but by its acquired ability to create and shape the need it alone can satisfy, and that the encroachment of such a monopoly can be pinpointed by social analysis while its limit is a matter of politics | Illich (1974), Energy and Equity, read in full in [NOTE-1913](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1913.md). | [THEORY-1864](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1864.md) | Ellul holds that technique, the totality of efficient methods and not machines alone, has become the milieu in which modern humans must live, autonomous, unified, universal and totalizing, progressing by self-augmentation and not yet able to correct its own errors, so that particular choices count for little | Ellul (1983 essay, posted introduction), read in [NOTE-1920](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1920.md). Technological pluralism; cosmotechnics; bifurcation of technological futures. A stand-in for the thesis of [LIT-2584](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2584.md). | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1867](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1867.md) | Moen argues that Kaczynski's case against industrial technology reaches its conclusion from defensible empirical worries, that technological progress is hard to predict and as an arms race hard to restrain, only through unargued evaluative premises that count technology's harms and not its benefits, so that counted even-handedly the case fails |  | Proposed |
